transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess I’ve just been under a lot of stress lately. My in-laws moved into our house, and since then I’ve felt really keyed up and worn down. I’m trying to handle it, but I’ve been snapping at my wife more than I should, and I’ve been avoiding calls I’d normally deal with right away.

I manage artists, so I can’t really afford to be scattered, but I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just… couldn’t think straight. That’s not like me. I thought it might be time to talk to someone, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a number of things, like work, family, or everyday responsibilities, even when there isn’t a clear problem?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s a number of things, exactly. I mean, I worry, sure, but it feels more tied to what’s going on at home and trying not to let it spill over. I don’t know if that counts as excessive. I don’t want to overstate it.
Do you feel like you have trouble controlling your worry, even when you try not to focus on it?

I don’t know… I mean, I can usually pull myself together when I need to, or at least I try to. It’s not like I’m sitting there panicking all day or anything.

But, yeah, sometimes when I try to put it out of my head, it sort of keeps coming back anyway. I’m not sure if that’s “trouble controlling it” exactly… does that make sense?
Have you noticed any physical signs or symptoms, like trouble sleeping, muscle tension, irritability, or feeling restless, especially when you're dealing with the stress at home?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I have felt really keyed up, especially when things at home are tense. And worn down, too.

The main thing I’ve noticed is I get irritable — I’ve been snapping at my wife, which I feel bad about. And I’ve been putting off calls I’d normally take care of right away. It’s like my head gets so crowded that I can’t think clearly. I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because of that, which… honestly scared me a bit. Does that fit with what you mean?
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like work or hobbies, even before the in-laws moved in?

Before they moved in? No, not really. I mean, I had normal stress, like anyone with work, but I was functioning fine. I was keeping up with things, enjoying my routine, handling responsibilities.

This all really started after my in-laws moved in — within a few weeks, I’d say. Once they kind of took over the house, that’s when I started feeling like I wasn’t myself. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you, in the past two weeks, felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d say “most of the day, nearly every day.” I’ve had some low moments, definitely, but depressed… I don’t know. I don’t want to overstate it.

It’s more like I get worn down when things pile up, and then I can still sort of push through. So… maybe not in the way you’re asking? Is that a fair answer?
Have you found it hard to concentrate on things, like work or reading, even before recent stressors at home?

No, before the home situation changed, I don’t think so. I was functioning pretty normally — work, reading, handling calls, all of that was okay.

This really seemed to start after my in-laws moved in and, I guess, sort of took over the house. Within a few weeks I noticed I wasn’t operating like myself. I hope that’s the kind of distinction you mean.
Would you say that your worry about things has felt persistent, even when you try to address or manage it?

Yes… I think persistent is probably fair. I’ve been trying to manage it, you know, tell myself it’s just a family situation and I should be able to handle it, but since my in-laws moved into the house I’ve felt really keyed up and worn down.

I don’t love admitting this, but it’s been affecting me more than I’d like. I’ve been snapping at my wife, and I’ve avoided some calls I normally would’ve handled right away. There was even a musician’s contract I almost let fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight. That’s not really like me. Does that answer what you mean by persistent?
Have you ever had sudden episodes where you felt intense anxiety, like a panic attack, where your heart raced, you felt short of breath, or feared something terrible was going to happen?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve felt really anxious and tense at times, but not like a sudden attack where I thought I was going to die or couldn’t breathe.

My heart might race a bit when I’m worked up, but I wouldn’t want to call it a panic attack if that’s not what it is. Is that the distinction you’re asking about?
Have you lost interest or felt less pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, like work or other things, since your in-laws moved in?

I’m not sure I’d say I’ve lost interest exactly. I still care about my work, and I still want to enjoy the usual things.

Maybe I’m just more distracted or not as into things in the moment, if that makes sense. But I don’t think it’s that I don’t enjoy anything anymore. Is that a reasonable way to put it?
Since your in-laws moved in, have you found that you no longer take pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even if you still know you should care about them?

I’m not sure I’d say “no longer take pleasure,” exactly. That feels a little stronger than what I mean.

It’s more like I’m distracted, or preoccupied, so I’m not as present with things I normally enjoy. But if I can actually settle into something, I think I can still get something out of it. I don’t want to overstate it, if that makes sense.
Would you say that, most days since your in-laws moved in, you’ve felt down or sad for much of the day, even if you’re not sure it’s full depression?

I don’t know if I’d call it “down or sad for much of the day,” exactly. I mean, I’ve had rough days, definitely, and I haven’t felt like myself.

But I’m a little hesitant to say it’s most of the day or most days. It’s more like this heaviness comes and goes, depending on what’s happening at home. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you, since your in-laws moved in, felt like you’re going through the motions with things you used to enjoy, like there’s no real pleasure or satisfaction in them anymore, even if you still try to do them?

I guess… not really in that “no real pleasure anymore” way. I mean, there are times I’m sort of just doing the thing and my mind is elsewhere, so it can probably look like I’m going through the motions.

But I wouldn’t want to say there’s no satisfaction at all. It’s more that I’m preoccupied and it takes more effort to enjoy things. Does that distinction make sense?
Have you found that you’re not interested in things at all anymore, even the ones you used to really enjoy, like work or hobbies?

I don’t think I’d say I’m not interested in things at all anymore. That sounds… pretty absolute, and I don’t think that’s quite it.

Work and hobbies still matter to me. I may be less focused or slower to get into them sometimes, but it’s not like I’ve stopped caring completely. Is that a fair way to put it?
Have you felt a noticeable loss of energy or felt fatigued almost every day since your in-laws moved in, even when you’re not physically tired?

Yeah… I think that part is probably fair to say. I’ve been really worn down since they moved in. I keep telling myself it’s just the house being crowded and stressful, but I’m keyed up all the time and then somehow exhausted too.

I don’t know if it’s “almost every day” in the clinical sense, but it feels pretty constant lately. I’m even avoiding calls I’d normally handle right away for work, and… I’m embarrassed to say this, but I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight. So yes, I guess there has been a noticeable loss of energy.
Have you had days where you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of at least two weeks since your in-laws moved in?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most of the day nearly every day, no. I’ve had some bad days, definitely, where I feel pretty low or discouraged, but I don’t know that it’s been that constant for two weeks straight.

I don’t want to minimize it, but I also don’t want to overstate it. It feels more like I get overwhelmed and dragged down by the situation, if that makes sense.
